```{r data read in and processing}
#| cache: true 
#| include: false

# --- accel data ----- # 
walking = read_rds(here::here("data", "walking.rds"))
driving = read_rds(here::here("data", "driving.rds"))
cooking = read_rds(here::here("data", "cooking.rds"))

# --- pa data --- # 
nh_pa = read_rds(here::here("data", "covariates_pa_valid.rds"))
nh_pa = nh_pa |> 
  filter(valid_accel, age_in_years_at_screening >= 18) |> 
  mutate(age_cat = cut(age_in_years_at_screening, breaks = c(18, 29, 39, 49, 59, 69, Inf), include.lowest = TRUE),
         age_cat = factor(age_cat, labels = c("18-29", "30-39", "40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70+"))) |> 
  rename(age = age_in_years_at_screening)


mims_sl = read_rds(here::here("data", "mims_covariates.rds"))
# add age cat
mims_sl = 
  mims_sl |> 
  filter(age_in_years_at_screening >= 18) |> 
   mutate(age_cat = cut(age_in_years_at_screening, breaks = c(18, 29, 39, 49, 59, 69, Inf), include.lowest = TRUE),
         age_cat = factor(age_cat, labels = c("18-29", "30-39", "40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70+"))) |> 
  left_join(nh_pa |> select(SEQN, mortstat, body_mass_index_kg_m_2), 
            by = "SEQN") |> 
  rename(age = age_in_years_at_screening, 
         bmi = body_mass_index_kg_m_2) |> 
  filter(!is.na(bmi), age >= 18)

df_tf = mims_sl %>%
  mutate(
    activity = tfd(as.matrix(select(., starts_with("min_"))), arg = seq(1/60, 24, length = 1440))) %>%
  select(SEQN, age, gender, bmi, activity)

```

### Regression in each bin?  

$$
\text{BMI}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{MIMS bin1}_i + \beta_2\text{MIMS bin2}_i + \dots + \beta_{12}\text{MIMS bin12}_i + \beta_{13}\text{age}_i + \beta_{14}\text{gender}_i + \epsilon_i
$$


<div style="font-size: 125%;">

```{r bin reg}

fit_binned = 
  lm(bmi ~ .,
     data = tf_spread(mims_binned |> select(-SEQN)))
```

### Regression in each bin? 

```{r bin reg plot }
p_bin = 
  fit_binned |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  filter(grepl("mims", term)) |> 
  mutate(hour = sub(".*mims\\_binned\\_", "", term),
         hour = as.numeric(hour),
         ub = estimate + 1.96 * std.error,
         lb = estimate - 1.96 * std.error) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = estimate)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = ub, ymin = lb), width = .5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 4),
                     labels = c("00:00", "04:00", "08:00", "12:00", "16:00", "20:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Coefficient (effect on BMI of increase in PA)", title = "Binned Regressions") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey")

p_bin

```


---

### Problems with binning


::: {.incremental}
+ Bin size arbitrary
+ As bins become smaller, coefficients over time become more different, but it's unclear if this is due to signal or noise
+ Solution: **scalar on function regression** (SoFR) 
+ We treat the physical activity predictor as a **smooth function over time** 
+ Let's do some math to make this connection 
:::

---

### Binning --> SoFR connection 

Define: 

$X_i(s_j)$: MIMS value at time $s_j$ for person $i$

$\bar{X}_{ib}$: Average MIMS in bin $b$ for person $i$ 

$\beta_b$: regression coefficient for bin $b$ in the previous model 

---

$\beta_b$: regression coefficient for bin $b$ in the previous model

---



### Binning --> SoFR connection 

Define: 

$X_i(s_j)$: MIMS value at time $s_j$ for person $i$

$\bar{X}_{ib}$: Average MIMS in bin $b$ for person $i$ 

**$\beta_b$: regression coefficient for bin $b$ in the previous model **

```{r bb}
fit_binned |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  filter(grepl("mims", term)) |> 
  mutate(hour = sub(".*mims\\_binned\\_", "", term),
         hour = as.numeric(hour),
         ub = estimate + 1.96 * std.error,
         lb = estimate - 1.96 * std.error) |> 
  mutate(col = hour == 1) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = estimate)) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_point(aes(color = col)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = ub, ymin = lb, color = col), width = .5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 4),
                     labels = c("00:00", "04:00", "08:00", "12:00", "16:00", "20:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Coefficient") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red")) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 1, y = -0.1, label = "beta[1]", parse = TRUE, size = 5, color = "red", family = "sans") 

```

---

### Binning --> SoFR connection 

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_1\bar{X}_{i1} &= \beta_1\frac{1}{120}\sum_{j=1}^{120}X_i(s_j) \\
&= \frac{\beta_1}{2}\Big[\frac{1}{60}\sum_{j=1}^{120}X_i(s_j)\Big] \\
&\approx \int_0^2\frac{\beta_1}{2}X_i(s)\,ds
\end{aligned}
$$
Last step: numeric approximation to true integral; emphasizing that $X_i(s_j)$ is a continuous function observed discretely

---

### Binning --> SoFR connection 

We could formalize this, defining function $\beta^{\text{step}}(s)$ as: 

$$
\beta^{\text{step}}(s) = \begin{cases} \frac{\beta_1}{2}, 0 < s \leq 2\\
\frac{\beta_2}{2}, 2 < s \leq 4\\
\dots \\
\frac{\beta_{12}}{2}, 22 < s \leq 24\\
\end{cases}
$$

In words: $\beta^{\text{step}}(s)$ is a step function with step heights equal to half of the bin coefficients

---

### Binning --> SoFR connection 

We can express the model using bin averages as a function of $\beta^{\text{step}}(s)$: 



$$
\sum_{b=1}^{12}\beta_b\bar{X}_{ib} \approx \int_0^{24}\beta^{\text{step}}(s)X_i(s)\,ds
$$

----

### Binning --> SoFR connection 

We can then plot these bin coefficients: 

```{r bin conn}
sf_coef_df = 
  fit_binned |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  filter(grepl("mims", term)) |> 
  mutate(hour = sub(".*mims\\_binned\\_", "", term),
         hour = as.numeric(hour),
         ub = estimate + 1.96 * std.error,
         lb = estimate - 1.96 * std.error) |>
  select(estimate, std.error) |> 
  slice(rep(1:12, each = 120)) |> 
  mutate(
    method = "Step",
    estimate = 0.5 * estimate,
    arg = seq(1/60, 24, length = 1440)) |> 
  tf_nest(.id = "method")
  
p_coef = 
  sf_coef_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = estimate)) + 
  geom_spaghetti(alpha = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 4),
                     labels = c("00:00", "04:00", "08:00", "12:00", "16:00", "20:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Coefficient") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") 

p_coef 
```

---

### What have we learned? 

We can obtain identical predicted BMI in two ways

1. Take average of predictors in each bin, regress BMI on these averages 
2. Integrate the product of the predictors (not binned) and the coefficient step function

### What have we learned? 

We can obtain identical predicted BMI in two ways

**2. Integrate the product of the predictors (not binned) and the coefficient step function**

### Simple linear scalar on function regression

We will extend the step coefficient approach to a more general functional coefficient

$$
Y_i = \beta_0 + \int_S\beta_1(s) X_i(s)ds + \epsilon_i
$$

Earlier, we required $\beta_1(s)$ to be a step function approximated by a regression model based on bin averages, now $\beta_1(s)$ is more flexible

---

### Simple linear scalar on function regression

We will extend the step coefficient approach to a more general functional coefficient

$$
Y_i = \beta_0 + \int_S\beta_1(s) X_i(s)ds + \epsilon_i
$$

Earlier, we required $\beta_1(s)$ to be a step function approximated by a regression model based on bin averages, now $\beta_1(s)$ is more flexible

Interpretation is the same: $\beta_1(s)$: weight of predictor function at each $s\in S$, product of $X_i(s)$ and $\beta_1(s)$ is integrated over $S$ to get the total contribution to the outcome of the functional term 

---

### Simple linear scalar on function regression

We will extend the step coefficient approach to a more general functional coefficient

$$
Y_i = \beta_0 + \int_S\beta_1(s) X_i(s)ds + \epsilon_i
$$

Earlier, we required $\beta_1(s)$ to be a step function approximated by a regression model based on bin averages, now $\beta_1(s)$ is more flexible

Interpretation is the same: $\beta_1(s)$: weight of predictor function at each $s\in S$, product of $X_i(s)$ and $\beta_1(s)$ is integrated over $S$ to get the total contribution to the outcome of the functional term 

$\beta_1(s)$: effect on outcome of one unit increase in $X_i(s)$ when all other values of $X_i(s'), s'\neq s$ are held constant (kind of awkward!)

---

### Simple linear scalar on function regression visualized

```{r prof plot}
quants = quantile(mims_mean$mean_mims, c(.01, .5, .95))


low_sub = 
  mims_mean |> 
  filter(round(mean_mims, 1) == round(quants[1], 1)) |> 
  slice(3) |> 
  pull(SEQN)


med_sub = 
  mims_mean |> 
  filter(round(mean_mims, 2) == round(quants[2], 2)) |> 
  slice(1) |> 
  pull(SEQN)


hi_sub = 
  mims_mean |> 
  filter(round(mean_mims, 2) == round(quants[3], 2)) |> 
  slice(5) |> 
  pull(SEQN)

profiles = 
  df_tf |> 
  filter(SEQN %in% c(low_sub, med_sub, hi_sub)) |> 
  mutate(SEQN = factor(SEQN, levels = c("67225", "63491", "78132"))) |> 
  # mutate(SEQN = glue::glue("ID {SEQN}, age = {age}, {gender}, BMI = {bmi}, mean MIMS = {med}")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = activity, color = SEQN)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c( "#2400D8", "#FF7856", "#A50021")) +
  geom_spaghetti(alpha = 1) +
  facet_grid(SEQN ~ .) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6),
                     labels = c("00:00", "06:00", "12:00", "18:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Physical Activity (MIMS)",
       title = expression(Three~ MIMS ~ profiles  ~ X[i](s))) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank())

profiles
```

### Simple linear scalar on function regression visualized


```{r coef plot}
#| cache: true
# get the functional coefficient
# get the product 
# get the integral 

mims_mat = mims_sl |> select(starts_with("min")) |> as.matrix()
nh_df = mims_sl |> select(-starts_with("min")) |> 
  mutate(mims_mat = mims_mat)
pfr_fit = 
  pfr(bmi ~ lf(mims_mat, argvals = seq(1, 1440, 1),
               bs = "ps", k = 30) + age + gender, 
              method = "REML", data = nh_df)

beta_hat = coef(pfr_fit, select = 1, coords = list(seq(1, 1440, 1)))

cplot = beta_hat |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = mims_mat.argvals, y = value)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1440, 6 * 60),
                     labels = c("00:00", "06:00", "12:00", "18:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Coefficient", title = expression(Functional~ Coefficient ~ beta[1](s))) +
  theme(title = element_text(family = "sans"))

cplot
```

### Simple linear scalar on function regression visualized


```{r prod vis}
#| cache: true 


df_temp =
  df_tf |> 
  filter(SEQN %in% c(low_sub, med_sub, hi_sub)) |> 
  tf_spread(activity) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("activity")) |> 
  group_by(SEQN) |> 
  mutate(num = row_number())

prod_df = 
  beta_hat |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  left_join(df_temp, by = join_by(mims_mat.argvals == num)) |> 
  mutate(prod = value.x * value.y)

seqn_levels = c("67225", "63491", "78132")

contribs = prod_df |> 
  group_by(SEQN) |> 
  summarize(contribution = sum(prod)) |> 
  mutate(
    SEQN  = factor(SEQN, levels = seqn_levels),
    label =  latex2exp::TeX(sprintf(r"($\int_S \beta_1(s)X_i(s)\,ds = %.2f$)", contribution),
                output = "character")

prod_plot =
```

### Estimation

How do we actually estimate $\beta_1(s)$? 

---

### Estimation

How do we actually estimate $\beta_1(s)$? 

Need to minimize: 

$$
\min_{\beta_0, \beta_1(s)}\sum_{i=1}^n\Big\{Y_i - \beta_0 - \int_S\beta_1(s)X_i(s)\,ds\Big\}^2
$$
